title.fr: Normes et certification (IREB CPRE, ISO/IEC 29148, IEEE 830)
title.en: Standards and certification (IREB CPRE, ISO/IEC 29148, IEEE 830)

hook.fr: Le diplôme CPRE, la norme ISO 29148 : exigence bien formée, 9 qualités, attributs, et les trois documents StRS / SyRS / SRS.
hook.en: The CPRE diploma and ISO 29148: well-formed requirement, 9 qualities, attributes, and the three documents StRS / SyRS / SRS.

text.fr: Un diplôme pour dire « je sais faire de l’IE »
text.en: A certificate to say "I can do RE"

text.fr: Dans un CV, comment prouver qu’on maîtrise l’ingénierie des exigences ? Le prof présente le **CPRE** (*Certified Professional for Requirements Engineering*), le diplôme de l’**IREB**. C’est un [[term-cpre|certificat personnel]] : il n’est pas limité dans le temps. Ses buts, tels que listés sur la diapo : établir une terminologie commune en IE, fournir des techniques et méthodes acceptées au niveau international, fournir une base de formation reconnue, et améliorer la pratique actuelle de l’IE.
text.en: On a CV, how do you prove you master requirements engineering? The teacher presents the **CPRE** (*Certified Professional for Requirements Engineering*), the diploma of the **IREB**. It is a [[term-cpre|personal certificate]]: it is not time limited. Its goals, as listed on the slide: establish a common terminology in RE, provide internationally accepted techniques and methods, provide an internationally accepted base for training, and improve the current practice of RE.

src.quote: Personal certificate for requirements engineering • not time limited
establish a common terminology in RE
provide international accepted techniques and methods for RE
provide an international accepted base for training in RE
improve the current practice of RE

text.fr: L’IREB (*International Requirements Engineering Board*) élabore les programmes (*curricula*), les examens et le **glossaire** du CPRE. Pour garantir équité et neutralité, les tâches sont réparties entre des organisations clairement séparées et indépendantes : l’IREB, les organismes de formation et les organismes de certification.
text.en: The IREB (International Requirements Engineering Board) produces the curricula, exams and the **glossary** of the CPRE. To guarantee fairness and neutrality, tasks are split between clearly separated and independent organizations: the IREB, the training providers and the certification bodies.

src.quote: Elaboration of the curriculi, exams and the glossary for the
Allocation of tasks to clearly separated and independent organizations ensures fairness and neutrality.

text.fr: Deux marches : Foundation puis Advanced
text.en: Two steps: Foundation, then Advanced

text.fr: La certification se fait en **deux étapes**. Le niveau **Foundation (FL)** donne une compréhension fondamentale du domaine, de la méthodologie et des techniques disponibles ; il est accessible à tous, **sans prérequis**. Le niveau **Advanced (AL)** consiste à maîtriser et utiliser méthodes et techniques, avec une spécialisation dans un ou plusieurs modules : *Requirements Elicitation and Consolidation*, *Requirements Modeling*, *Requirements Management* (ce dernier « en cours » sur la diapo).
text.en: Certification has **two steps**. The **Foundation Level (FL)** gives a fundamental understanding of the domain, the methodology and the available techniques; it is open to everyone, with **no prerequisites**. The **Advanced Level (AL)** means mastering and using methods and techniques, with a specialization in one or more modules: *Requirements Elicitation and Consolidation*, *Requirements Modeling*, *Requirements Management* (the latter "in work" on the slide).

src.quote: Two step certification program
CPRE Foundation Level • accessible to everyone, as there are no prerequisites
Fundamental understanding of domain, methodology and available techniques
Mastering and using methods and techniques
Specialization in one or more modules

text.fr: La norme ISO/IEC 29148 : le « mode d’emploi » international
text.en: ISO/IEC 29148: the international "user manual"

text.fr: Et si l’on veut une référence officielle sur *comment* faire de l’IE ? C’est la norme **ISO/IEC 29148** (*Requirements engineering*, dans la série « processus du cycle de vie »). Elle traite de façon unifiée les processus et les produits de l’ingénierie des exigences sur tout le cycle de vie des systèmes et logiciels. Elle **harmonise** plusieurs sources, dont ISO/IEC 12207, ISO/IEC 15288 et… l’**IEEE Std 830**, la pratique recommandée pour les spécifications d’exigences logicielles.
text.en: What if you want an official reference on *how* to do RE? That is **ISO/IEC 29148** (*Requirements engineering*, in the "life cycle processes" series). It gives a unified treatment of the processes and products of requirements engineering throughout the life cycle of systems and software. It **harmonizes** several sources, including ISO/IEC 12207, ISO/IEC 15288 and the **IEEE Std 830**, the recommended practice for software requirements specifications.

src.quote: This International Standard provides a unified treatment of the processes and products involved in engineering requirements throughout the life cycle of systems and software.
IEEE Std 830, IEEE Recommended Practice for Software Requirements Specifications

text.fr: Elle fournit deux choses : des **processus** normatifs avec des conseils d’application, et une spécification normative du **contenu des documents** (« information items ») produits par ces processus. On peut revendiquer la conformité aux processus, à la documentation, ou aux deux (*full conformance*).
text.en: It provides two things: normative **processes** with guidance on implementing them, and a normative specification of the **content of the documents** ("information items") produced by these processes. One can claim conformance to the processes, to the documentation, or to both (*full conformance*).

src.quote: normative processes and exemplary guidance on implementing the requirements-related processes
normative specification of the contents of the information items produced through the implementation of these processes
Users of this International Standard can claim conformance to the process provisions or to the documentation provisions, or both.

text.fr: Du besoin à l’exigence « bien formée »
text.en: From a need to a "well-formed" requirement

text.fr: Un client dit : « Je veux un système rapide ». Est-ce déjà une exigence ? Non, répond la norme : une première expression de l’intention des parties prenantes n’est pas forcément une exigence, car elle n’a été ni définie, ni analysée, ni jugée réalisable. Ce sont des **besoins**, buts ou objectifs. Le but de l’IE est de les traduire en un **ensemble cohérent d’exigences bien formées**.
text.en: A client says: "I want a fast system". Is that already a requirement? No, says the standard: a first statement of stakeholders’ intention is not necessarily a requirement, because it has not been defined, analyzed, nor ensured to be feasible. These are **needs**, goals or objectives. The purpose of RE is to translate them into an **integrated and coherent set of well-formed requirements**.

src.quote: An initial presentation of stakeholders’ intention is not necessarily a requirement since it has not been defined, analyzed, nor ensured to be feasible.
the key purpose of the requirements engineering activity is to translate all stakeholder needs into a integrated and coherent set of well-formed requirements.

text.fr: Une exigence [[term-wellformed|bien formée]] est un énoncé qui : (1) peut être **vérifié** ; (2) doit être satisfait par le système pour résoudre un problème ou atteindre un objectif d’une partie prenante ; (3) est qualifié par des conditions mesurables et borné par des contraintes. En langage naturel, l’énoncé comprend **un sujet, un verbe et un complément**.
text.en: A [[term-wellformed|well-formed]] requirement is a statement that: (1) can be **verified**; (2) must be met by the system to solve a stakeholder problem or achieve a stakeholder objective; (3) is qualified by measurable conditions and bounded by constraints. In natural language, the statement comprises **a subject, a verb and a complement**.

src.quote: A well-formed requirement is a statement of system or system element characteristics that:
Must be met or possessed by a system to solve a stakeholder problem or to achieve a stakeholder objective
Is qualified by measurable conditions and bounded by constraints.
the statement should comprise a subject, a verb and a complement.

text.fr: Pour savoir ce qui est obligatoire, la norme propose de convenir à l’avance de mots-clés. Ils doivent être définis formellement et appliqués de façon cohérente dans toutes les exigences du projet.
text.en: To tell what is binding, the standard suggests agreeing on keywords in advance. They must be formally defined and applied consistently across all the project’s requirements.

src.quote: Whatever keywords and terms are used should be formally defined and applied consistently throughout all requirements on the system/software development project

rows.fr: Fait, futur ou déclaration d’intention : non obligatoire. À éviter pour une exigence (peut être lu comme juridiquement contraignant)
rows.en: Fact, futurity or declaration of purpose: non-mandatory. Best avoided for requirements (can be construed as legally binding)

rows.fr: Préférence ou but : souhaité, non obligatoire

src.quote: Requirements are mandatory binding provisions and use 'shall'.
Statements of fact, futurity, or a declaration of purpose are non-mandatory, no-binding provisions and use 'will'.
Preferences or goals are desired, non-mandatory, non-binding provisions and use 'should'.
Suggestions or allowances are non-mandatory, non-binding provisions and use 'may'.

text.fr: **Réflexe d’examen** : écrire « Le système **doit**… » (*shall*), avec un sujet (le système), un verbe d’action et un complément mesurable. Un besoin du type « rapide » ou « convivial » n’est pas encore une exigence bien formée.
text.en: **Exam reflex**: write "The system **shall**…", with a subject (the system), an action verb and a measurable complement. A need like "fast" or "friendly" is not yet a well-formed requirement.

src.quote: Requirements are mandatory binding provisions and use 'shall'.
Is qualified by measurable conditions and bounded by constraints.
the statement should comprise a subject, a verb and a complement.

text.fr: Neuf qualités pour une exigence, quatre pour un ensemble
text.en: Nine qualities for one requirement, four for a set

text.fr: La norme dresse la liste des **caractéristiques d’une exigence individuelle**. Chacune devient une grille de relecture : quand on critique une exigence, on nomme la caractéristique qui lui manque.
text.en: The standard lists the **characteristics of an individual requirement**. Each one becomes a review checklist: when criticizing a requirement, name the characteristic it lacks.

src.quote: Necessary. The requirement defines an essential capability characteristic, constraint, and/or quality factor.

rows.fr: Définit une capacité, contrainte ou qualité essentielle ; si on la supprime, il manque quelque chose
rows.en: Defines an essential capability, constraint or quality factor; removing it leaves a deficiency
Implementation independent: states what, not how

rows.fr: Une seule interprétation possible, énoncé simple
rows.en: Can be interpreted in only one way; stated simply

rows.fr: Sans conflit avec les autres exigences
rows.en: Free of conflicts with other requirements

rows.fr: Complète, mesurable, sans besoin de précision supplémentaire
rows.en: Complete, measurable, needs no further amplification

rows.fr: **Une seule** exigence par énoncé, sans conjonction
rows.en: Only **one** requirement, no use of conjunctions

rows.fr: Techniquement faisable, dans le budget, le calendrier et les contraintes
rows.en: Technically feasible, within budget, schedule and other constraints

rows.fr: Reliée vers le haut (besoin, exigence de niveau supérieur) et vers le bas (exigences de niveau inférieur)
rows.en: Traced upwards to its source and downwards to lower-tier requirements

rows.fr: On dispose d’un moyen de prouver que le système la satisfait ; elle est mesurable
rows.en: There is a means to prove the system satisfies it; it is measurable

src.quote: Necessary. The requirement defines an essential capability characteristic, constraint, and/or quality factor.
Abstract. Each requirement should be implementation independent. The requirement states what is required, not how the requirement should be met.
Unambiguous. Each requirement should be stated in such a way so that it can be interpreted in only one way.
Consistent. The requirement is free of conflicts with other requirements.
Complete. The stated requirement is complete, measurable and does not need further amplification.
Concise. The requirement statement includes only one requirement with no use of conjunctions.
Feasible. The requirement must be technically feasible and fit within budget, schedule, available technology, and other constraints.
Traceable. Each requirement should be traced upwards to specific documented stakeholder statement(s) of need, higher tier requirement, or other source
Each requirement should also be traced downwards to the specific requirements in the lower tier requirements specification or other system definition artifacts.
Verifiable. Each requirement should have the means to prove that the system satisfies the specified requirement. An attribute of being verifiable is that the requirement is measurable.

text.fr: **Pièges** : « concise » = pas de « et » qui cache deux exigences ; « abstraite » = pas de solution technique imposée (le *comment*) ; « vérifiable » = mesurable. Ce sont les défauts à nommer quand on critique une exigence.
text.en: **Traps**: "concise" = no "and" hiding two requirements; "abstract" = no imposed technical solution (the *how*); "verifiable" = measurable. These are the defects to name when criticizing a requirement.

src.quote: Concise. The requirement statement includes only one requirement with no use of conjunctions.
Abstract. Each requirement should be implementation independent. The requirement states what is required, not how the requirement should be met.
Verifiable. Each requirement should have the means to prove that the system satisfies the specified requirement. An attribute of being verifiable is that the requirement is measurable.

text.fr: Une bonne exigence ne suffit pas : l’**ensemble** doit lui aussi tenir. Il est **complet** (aucun « à définir » : TBD, TBS, TBR), **cohérent** (pas de contradiction, pas de doublon, un même terme pour une même chose), **abordable** (réalisable dans les coûts, délais et contraintes techniques) et **borné** (il reste dans le périmètre de la solution visée). Vérifier ces points évite la dérive des exigences (*requirements creep*).
text.en: A good requirement is not enough: the **set** must hold too. It is **complete** (no "to be defined": TBD, TBS, TBR), **consistent** (no contradiction, no duplicate, one term for one item), **affordable** (achievable within cost, schedule and technical constraints) and **bounded** (it stays within the scope of the intended solution). Checking these points avoids requirements creep.

src.quote: The final set of requirements can be judged complete when no TBx are present.
Consistent. The set of requirements does not have individual requirements which are contradictory. Requirements are not duplicated. The same term is used for the same item in all requirements.
Affordable. The complete set of requirements can be satisfied by a solution that is obtainable within lifecycle cost, schedule, and technical constraints.
Bounded. The set of requirements maintains the identified scope for the intended solution without increasing beyond what is needed to satisfy user needs.
Careful checking of the requirements set for these characteristics is critical to avoiding requirements changes and growth (“requirements creep”)

text.fr: Écrire sans flou : les mots à bannir
text.en: Writing without vagueness: words to avoid

text.fr: La règle d’or de la norme : une exigence dit **ce qu’il faut** (*what*), pas **comment** le faire (*how*). Y glisser une décision de conception risque d’écarter d’autres solutions. L’information utile peut vivre ailleurs, par exemple dans l’attribut « justification ». La norme demande aussi d’éviter les termes vagues, qui rendent l’exigence invérifiable ou interprétable de plusieurs façons.
text.en: The standard’s golden rule: a requirement states **what** is needed, not **how**. Slipping in a design decision may rule out other solutions. Useful information can live elsewhere, for example in the "rationale" attribute. The standard also asks to avoid vague terms, which make a requirement unverifiable or open to several readings.

src.quote: Requirements should state 'what' is needed, not 'how".
Avoid terms that are vague and general.

rows.fr: "provide support", "but not limited to", "as a minimum"
rows.en: "provide support", "but not limited to", "as a minimum"

src.quote: Superlatives (such as "best", "most")
Subjective language (such as "user friendly", "easy to use", "cost effective")
Vague pronouns (such as "it", "this", "that")
Ambiguous adverbs and adjectives (such as "almost always", "significant", "minimal")
Open-ended, non-verifiable terms (such as "provide support", "but not limited to", "as a minimum")
Comparative phrases (such as "better than", "higher quality")
Loopholes (such as "if possible", "as appropriate", "as applicable")

text.fr: Les attributs : la carte d’identité d’une exigence
text.en: Attributes: a requirement’s ID card

text.fr: Une exigence bien formée est aussi **catégorisée** par des attributs, généralement stockés dans une base ou un outil d’exigences. Premier attribut, et le plus important pour la suite du cours : l’**identification**. Chaque exigence a un identifiant **unique** (numéro, étiquette, mnémonique…). Une fois attribué, il n’est **jamais modifié** (même si l’exigence change) et **jamais réutilisé** (même si l’exigence est supprimée).
text.en: A well-formed requirement is also **categorized** with attributes, usually kept in a database or requirements tool. The first attribute, and the key one for the rest of the course, is **identification**. Each requirement has a **unique** identifier (number, name tag, mnemonic…). Once assigned, it is **never changed** (even if the requirement changes) and **never reused** (even if the requirement is deleted).

src.quote: Categorization is usually achieved by attributes associated with the requirement in databases or other requirements tools.
Identification. Each requirement should be uniquely identified (i.e., number, name tag, mnemonic, buttons, hypertext).
Once assigned, the identification must be unique - it is never changed (even if the identified requirement changes) nor is it reused (even if the identified requirement is deleted).

rows.fr: Quelles exigences peuvent être négociées ; ne signifie pas que les autres sont inutiles
rows.en: Which requirements are candidates for trade-offs; does not mean the others are unnecessary

rows.fr: Une exigence peu prioritaire pour une partie prenante peut pourtant être essentielle au succès du système
rows.en: A requirement with low priority for one stakeholder may still be essential to the system’s success

rows.fr: Gradation des exigences par analyse de risque
rows.en: Grading of requirements through risk analysis

rows.fr: Qui est l’émetteur : on sait qui consulter en cas de conflit ou de modification
rows.en: Who originated it: tells whom to consult if unclear, conflicting or changing

rows.fr: La raison pour laquelle l’exigence existe
rows.en: The reason the requirement is needed

src.quote: Priority. The priority of each requirement should be identified.
The priority is not intended to imply that some requirements are not necessary
Criticality. The criticality of each requirement should be defined.
Some requirements could have a low priority from one of the stakeholder's perspective, but nevertheless be essential for the success of the system.
Risk. Risk analysis techniques can be used to determine a grading for system requirements.
Source. Each requirement should be further classified by a label that indicates the originator.
Rationale. The rationale for establishing each requirement should be captured.

text.fr: **Question probable** : « Priorité » ≠ « criticité ». La priorité sert à arbitrer ; la criticité dit qu’une exigence peu prioritaire peut pourtant être indispensable. Et un identifiant n’est jamais réutilisé, même après suppression.
text.en: **Likely question**: "priority" ≠ "criticality". Priority is for trade-offs; criticality says a low-priority requirement can still be essential. And an identifier is never reused, even after deletion.

src.quote: The priority is not intended to imply that some requirements are not necessary
Some requirements could have a low priority from one of the stakeholder's perspective, but nevertheless be essential for the success of the system.
Once assigned, the identification must be unique - it is never changed (even if the identified requirement changes) nor is it reused (even if the identified requirement is deleted).

text.fr: Trois documents pour trois niveaux : StRS, SyRS, SRS
text.en: Three documents for three levels: StRS, SyRS, SRS

text.fr: La norme définit le contenu de **trois spécifications** qui correspondent à trois niveaux d’exigences. La **StRS** (*Stakeholder Requirements Specification*) porte les exigences de gestion et d’exploitation de l’entreprise ; la **SyRS** (*System Requirements Specification*), les exigences système ; la **SRS** (*Software Requirements Specification*), les exigences logicielles.
text.en: The standard defines the content of **three specifications** matching three levels of requirements. The **StRS** (*Stakeholder Requirements Specification*) holds the business management and business operational requirements; the **SyRS** (*System Requirements Specification*), the system requirements; the **SRS** (*Software Requirements Specification*), the software requirements.

src.quote: This clause defines the required content of the stakeholder requirements specification (StRS), the system requirements specification (SyRS), and the software requirements specification (SRS).

The StRS, SyRS and SRS correspond to the requirement types in Figure 4 as Business Management Requirements and Business Operational Requirements, System Requirements, and Software Requirements, respectively.

rows.fr: Dit **pourquoi** on développe ou modifie le système (motivation métier) ; contenu sous la responsabilité des parties prenantes ; appelée BRS dans beaucoup de secteurs
rows.en: Says **why** the system is developed or changed (business motivation); content is the stakeholders’ responsibility; called BRS in many industries

rows.fr: Description « boîte noire » de ce que fait le système, via ses interactions et interfaces avec l’environnement ; pont entre client et équipe technique, lisible par les deux
rows.en: "Black-box" description of what the system should do through its interactions and interfaces with the environment; a bridge between customer and technical community, understandable by both

rows.fr: Exigences logicielles, au niveau de détail utile aux concepteurs et aux testeurs
rows.en: Software requirements, detailed enough for designers and for testers

src.quote: The StRS describes the business motivation for why the system is being developed or changed.
The stakeholder/customer should be responsible for the content of the specification.
The StRS is known as Business Requirement Specification (BRS) in many industries.

The purpose of the system requirements specification (SyRS) is to provide a "black-box" description of what the system should do, in terms of the system's interactions or interfaces with its external environment.

The collection of requirements that constitutes the specification and its representation acts as the bridge between the two groups and must be understandable by both the customer and the technical community.
The specific requirements clause of the SRS shall contain all of the software requirements to a level of detail sufficient to enable designers to design a system to satisfy those requirements.
The specific requirements clause of the SRS shall contain all of the software requirements to a level of detail sufficient to enable testers to test that the system satisfies those requirements.

text.fr: La **SRS** est l’héritière directe de l’IEEE 830 : c’est le « plan type » du cahier des charges logiciel. La section 1 est l’introduction (but, périmètre, définitions-acronymes-abréviations, références, vue d’ensemble). La section 2 est la description générale (dont les fonctions du produit). La section 3 contient les **exigences spécifiques**.
text.en: The **SRS** is the direct heir of IEEE 830: it is the "standard outline" of the software requirements document. Section 1 is the introduction (purpose, scope, definitions-acronyms-abbreviations, references, overview). Section 2 is the overall description (including product functions). Section 3 holds the **specific requirements**.

src.quote: IEEE Std 830, IEEE Recommended Practice for Software Requirements Specifications
The introduction of the SRS shall contain the following subsections:
Definitions, acronyms, and abbreviations;
Product functions (section 2.2 of the SRS)
at a minimum contain a description of every input (stimulus) into the system, every output (response) from the system, and all functions performed by the system

items.fr: assez détaillées pour que les concepteurs conçoivent et que les testeurs testent ;
items.en: detailed enough for designers to design and for testers to test;

items.fr: **perceptibles de l’extérieur** (utilisateurs, opérateurs ou systèmes externes) ;
items.en: **externally perceivable** by users, operators or external systems;

items.fr: décrire au minimum chaque entrée (stimulus), chaque sortie (réponse) et chaque fonction du système.
items.en: describe at least every input (stimulus), every output (response) and every function of the system.

src.quote: The specific requirements clause of the SRS shall contain all of the software requirements to a level of detail sufficient to enable designers to design a system to satisfy those requirements.
The specific requirements clause of the SRS shall contain all of the software requirements to a level of detail sufficient to enable testers to test that the system satisfies those requirements.
Every stated requirement in the specific requirements clause of the SRS shall be externally perceivable by users, operators, or other external systems.
Each requirement shall be uniquely identifiable.
at a minimum contain a description of every input (stimulus) into the system, every output (response) from the system, and all functions performed by the system

text.fr: **À retenir pour l’examen** : l’IEEE 830 structure le cahier des charges logiciel ; l’ISO 29148 l’intègre (SRS) et ajoute deux niveaux au-dessus (StRS, SyRS). Dans la SRS, chaque exigence spécifique doit être « externalement perceptible » et identifiable de façon unique.
text.en: **Exam reminder**: IEEE 830 structures the software requirements document; ISO 29148 integrates it (SRS) and adds two levels above (StRS, SyRS). In the SRS, every specific requirement must be externally perceivable and uniquely identifiable.

src.quote: IEEE Std 830, IEEE Recommended Practice for Software Requirements Specifications

The StRS, SyRS and SRS correspond to the requirement types in Figure 4 as Business Management Requirements and Business Operational Requirements, System Requirements, and Software Requirements, respectively.
Every stated requirement in the specific requirements clause of the SRS shall be externally perceivable by users, operators, or other external systems.
Each requirement shall be uniquely identifiable.

src.quote: A well-formed requirement is a statement of system or system element characteristics that:
Must be met or possessed by a system to solve a stakeholder problem or to achieve a stakeholder objective
Is qualified by measurable conditions and bounded by constraints.

definition.fr: Mot-clé qui signale une exigence : disposition obligatoire et contraignante. « should » exprime une préférence, « may » une autorisation, « will » un fait ou une intention.
definition.en: Keyword signalling a requirement: a mandatory, binding provision. "should" expresses a preference, "may" an allowance, "will" a fact or purpose.

src.quote: Requirements are mandatory binding provisions and use 'shall'.
Preferences or goals are desired, non-mandatory, non-binding provisions and use 'should'.
Suggestions or allowances are non-mandatory, non-binding provisions and use 'may'.
Statements of fact, futurity, or a declaration of purpose are non-mandatory, no-binding provisions and use 'will'.

definition.fr: Exigence reliée vers le haut à un besoin, une exigence de niveau supérieur ou une autre source, et vers le bas aux exigences de niveau inférieur.
definition.en: A requirement traced upwards to a stakeholder need, a higher-tier requirement or another source, and downwards to lower-tier requirements.

src.quote: Traceable. Each requirement should be traced upwards to specific documented stakeholder statement(s) of need, higher tier requirement, or other source
Each requirement should also be traced downwards to the specific requirements in the lower tier requirements specification or other system definition artifacts.

definition.fr: L’énoncé contient une seule exigence, sans conjonction.
definition.en: The statement includes only one requirement, with no use of conjunctions.

src.quote: Concise. The requirement statement includes only one requirement with no use of conjunctions.

definition.fr: Indépendante de l’implémentation : elle dit ce qui est requis, pas comment y répondre.
definition.en: Implementation independent: it states what is required, not how to meet it.

src.quote: Abstract. Each requirement should be implementation independent. The requirement states what is required, not how the requirement should be met.

definition.fr: « À définir », « à spécifier », « à résoudre » : un ensemble d’exigences est complet quand il n’en contient plus.
definition.en: "To Be Defined", "To Be Specified", "To Be Resolved": a set of requirements is complete when none is left.

src.quote: The final set of requirements can be judged complete when no TBx are present.

definition.fr: Croissance non maîtrisée des exigences en cours de projet, qui pèse sur le coût, le calendrier ou la qualité ; la vérification de l’ensemble des exigences permet de l’éviter.
definition.en: Uncontrolled growth and change of requirements during development, impacting cost, schedule or quality; careful checking of the requirements set helps avoid it.

src.quote: Careful checking of the requirements set for these characteristics is critical to avoiding requirements changes and growth (“requirements creep”)

definition.fr: Attribut : chaque exigence a un identifiant unique, jamais modifié ni réutilisé.
definition.en: Attribute: each requirement has a unique identifier, never changed nor reused.

src.quote: Identification. Each requirement should be uniquely identified (i.e., number, name tag, mnemonic, buttons, hypertext).
Once assigned, the identification must be unique - it is never changed (even if the identified requirement changes) nor is it reused (even if the identified requirement is deleted).

definition.fr: Attribut qui signale qu’une exigence, même de faible priorité pour une partie prenante, peut être essentielle au succès du système.
definition.en: Attribute showing that a requirement, even of low priority for one stakeholder, may be essential for the system’s success.

src.quote: Criticality. The criticality of each requirement should be defined.
Some requirements could have a low priority from one of the stakeholder's perspective, but nevertheless be essential for the success of the system.

definition.fr: Stakeholder Requirements Specification : décrit la motivation métier du développement ou de la modification du système ; contenu sous la responsabilité des parties prenantes (appelée BRS dans beaucoup de secteurs).
definition.en: Stakeholder Requirements Specification: describes the business motivation for developing or changing the system; stakeholders are responsible for its content (called BRS in many industries).

src.quote: The StRS describes the business motivation for why the system is being developed or changed.
The stakeholder/customer should be responsible for the content of the specification.
The StRS is known as Business Requirement Specification (BRS) in many industries.

definition.fr: System Requirements Specification : description « boîte noire » de ce que le système doit faire, par ses interactions avec son environnement.
definition.en: System Requirements Specification: a "black-box" description of what the system should do, in terms of its interactions with the external environment.

src.quote: The purpose of the system requirements specification (SyRS) is to provide a "black-box" description of what the system should do, in terms of the system's interactions or interfaces with its external environment.

definition.fr: Software Requirements Specification : spécification des exigences logicielles, structurée en introduction, description générale et exigences spécifiques.
definition.en: Software Requirements Specification: the specification of software requirements, structured as introduction, overall description and specific requirements.

src.quote: This clause defines the required content of the stakeholder requirements specification (StRS), the system requirements specification (SyRS), and the software requirements specification (SRS).
The introduction of the SRS shall contain the following subsections:
The specific requirements clause of the SRS shall contain all of the software requirements to a level of detail sufficient to enable designers to design a system to satisfy those requirements.

text.fr: CPRE de l’IREB : certificat personnel, non limité dans le temps, en deux niveaux (Foundation sans prérequis, Advanced avec modules de spécialisation).
text.en: IREB’s CPRE: personal, not time limited certificate, two levels (Foundation with no prerequisites, Advanced with specialization modules).

src.quote: Personal certificate for requirements engineering • not time limited

text.fr: Un besoin n’est pas une exigence : l’IE traduit les besoins en exigences bien formées (vérifiables, mesurables, bornées ; sujet + verbe + complément ; « shall »).
text.en: A need is not a requirement: RE translates needs into well-formed requirements (verifiable, measurable, bounded; subject + verb + complement; "shall").

src.quote: An initial presentation of stakeholders’ intention is not necessarily a requirement since it has not been defined, analyzed, nor ensured to be feasible.
the key purpose of the requirements engineering activity is to translate all stakeholder needs into a integrated and coherent set of well-formed requirements.
A well-formed requirement is a statement of system or system element characteristics that:
Is qualified by measurable conditions and bounded by constraints.
the statement should comprise a subject, a verb and a complement.
Requirements are mandatory binding provisions and use 'shall'.

text.fr: Neuf caractéristiques d’une exigence : nécessaire, abstraite, non ambiguë, cohérente, complète, concise, réalisable, traçable, vérifiable.
text.en: Nine characteristics of a requirement: necessary, abstract, unambiguous, consistent, complete, concise, feasible, traceable, verifiable.

src.quote: Necessary. The requirement defines an essential capability characteristic, constraint, and/or quality factor.
Abstract. Each requirement should be implementation independent. The requirement states what is required, not how the requirement should be met.
Unambiguous. Each requirement should be stated in such a way so that it can be interpreted in only one way.
Consistent. The requirement is free of conflicts with other requirements.
Complete. The stated requirement is complete, measurable and does not need further amplification.
Concise. The requirement statement includes only one requirement with no use of conjunctions.
Feasible. The requirement must be technically feasible and fit within budget, schedule, available technology, and other constraints.
Traceable. Each requirement should be traced upwards to specific documented stakeholder statement(s) of need, higher tier requirement, or other source
Verifiable. Each requirement should have the means to prove that the system satisfies the specified requirement. An attribute of being verifiable is that the requirement is measurable.

text.fr: Un ensemble d’exigences est complet (sans TBx), cohérent, abordable et borné.
text.en: A set of requirements is complete (no TBx), consistent, affordable and bounded.

src.quote: The final set of requirements can be judged complete when no TBx are present.
Consistent. The set of requirements does not have individual requirements which are contradictory. Requirements are not duplicated. The same term is used for the same item in all requirements.
Affordable. The complete set of requirements can be satisfied by a solution that is obtainable within lifecycle cost, schedule, and technical constraints.
Bounded. The set of requirements maintains the identified scope for the intended solution without increasing beyond what is needed to satisfy user needs.

text.fr: Dire *quoi*, pas *comment* ; bannir superlatifs, langage subjectif, pronoms vagues, comparatifs et échappatoires.
text.en: State what, not how; avoid superlatives, subjective language, vague pronouns, comparatives and loopholes.

src.quote: Requirements should state 'what' is needed, not 'how".
Superlatives (such as "best", "most")
Subjective language (such as "user friendly", "easy to use", "cost effective")
Vague pronouns (such as "it", "this", "that")
Comparative phrases (such as "better than", "higher quality")
Loopholes (such as "if possible", "as appropriate", "as applicable")

text.fr: Attributs : identification unique jamais modifiée ni réutilisée, priorité, criticité, risque, source, justification.
text.en: Attributes: unique identification never changed nor reused, priority, criticality, risk, source, rationale.

src.quote: Identification. Each requirement should be uniquely identified (i.e., number, name tag, mnemonic, buttons, hypertext).
Once assigned, the identification must be unique - it is never changed (even if the identified requirement changes) nor is it reused (even if the identified requirement is deleted).
Priority. The priority of each requirement should be identified.
Criticality. The criticality of each requirement should be defined.
Risk. Risk analysis techniques can be used to determine a grading for system requirements.
Source. Each requirement should be further classified by a label that indicates the originator.
Rationale. The rationale for establishing each requirement should be captured.

text.fr: Trois spécifications : StRS (pourquoi, côté métier), SyRS (boîte noire du système), SRS (logiciel) ; la SRS correspond au plan type de l’IEEE 830.
text.en: Three specifications: StRS (why, business side), SyRS (system black box), SRS (software); the SRS matches the IEEE 830 outline.

src.quote: The StRS, SyRS and SRS correspond to the requirement types in Figure 4 as Business Management Requirements and Business Operational Requirements, System Requirements, and Software Requirements, respectively.

statement.fr: L'IREB élabore les programmes, les examens et le glossaire du CPRE et délivre lui-même les certifications, ce qui assure l'équité et la neutralité du dispositif.
statement.en: The IREB develops the CPRE curricula, exams and glossary and itself issues the certificates, which provides fairness and neutrality for the scheme.

justification.fr: FAUX : l'IREB élabore programmes, examens et glossaire, mais les tâches sont **réparties entre des organisations clairement séparées et indépendantes** (IREB, organismes de formation, organismes de certification) : c'est cette séparation qui garantit équité et neutralité.
justification.en: FALSE: the IREB develops curricula, exams and glossary, but tasks are **allocated to clearly separated and independent organizations** (IREB, training bodies, certification bodies): this separation ensures fairness and neutrality.

statement.en: The CPRE is a two-step programme: the Foundation Level is open to everyone with no prerequisites, and the Advanced Level is about mastering methods and techniques, with a specialization in one or more modules.

justification.fr: VRAI : c'est la structure du programme présentée dans le cours (Foundation sans prérequis ; Advanced = maîtrise et spécialisation par modules).
justification.en: TRUE: this is the programme structure shown in the course (Foundation with no prerequisites; Advanced = mastery and specialization by modules).

src.quote: Two step certification program
CPRE Foundation Level • accessible to everyone, as there are no prerequisites

statement.fr: Le document ISO/IEC 29148 fourni dans le cours est la norme internationale ISO publiée, qu'on peut donc citer comme telle dans un cahier des charges.
statement.en: The ISO/IEC 29148 document supplied in the course is the published ISO International Standard, so it can be cited as such in a requirements specification.

justification.fr: FAUX : le fichier est un **Committee Draft** de 2009 qui précise « This document is not an ISO International Standard. It is distributed for review and comment. » Ses contenus sont ceux d'un brouillon.
justification.en: FALSE: the file is a 2009 **Committee Draft** stating "This document is not an ISO International Standard. It is distributed for review and comment." Its contents are those of a draft.

src.quote: This document is not an ISO International Standard. It is distributed for review and comment.

statement.fr: Dans la norme ISO/IEC 29148, le mot-clé « will » signale une exigence obligatoire et contraignante, alors que « should » exprime une simple préférence.
statement.en: In ISO/IEC 29148, the keyword "will" marks a mandatory, binding requirement, whereas "should" expresses a mere preference.

justification.fr: FAUX : l'exigence obligatoire s'écrit avec **« shall »**. « Will » exprime un fait, un futur ou une déclaration d'intention (non obligatoire) ; « should » une préférence ; « may » une suggestion.
justification.en: FALSE: a mandatory requirement uses **"shall"**. "Will" expresses a fact, futurity or a declaration of purpose (non-mandatory); "should" a preference; "may" a suggestion.

src.quote: Requirements are mandatory binding provisions and use 'shall'.

question.fr: Laquelle de ces phrases est une exigence bien formée au sens de la norme (sujet, verbe, complément mesurable, mot-clé d'exigence) ?
question.en: Which of these sentences is a well-formed requirement according to the standard (subject, verb, measurable complement, requirement keyword)?

options.fr: Le système doit offrir une interface rapide et agréable à tous les utilisateurs.
options.en: The system shall offer a fast and pleasant interface to all users.

options.fr: Le système devrait idéalement afficher la liste des commandes d'un client en moins de 2 secondes.
options.en: The system should ideally display a customer's order list in under 2 seconds.

options.fr: Le système affichera la liste des commandes d'un client en moins de 2 secondes pour 95 % des requêtes de consultation.
options.en: The system will display a customer's order list in under 2 seconds for 95% of lookup requests.

options.fr: Le système doit afficher la liste des commandes d'un client en moins de 2 secondes pour 95 % des requêtes.
options.en: The system shall display a customer's order list in under 2 seconds for 95% of requests.

explanation.fr: Seule la dernière a un **sujet, un verbe et un complément mesurable** avec **« shall »**. La 1re est subjective et non mesurable ; « should » exprime une préférence ; « will » une intention, non obligatoire.
explanation.en: Only the last one has a **subject, a verb and a measurable complement** with **"shall"**. The 1st is subjective and not measurable; "should" expresses a preference; "will" an intention, not mandatory.

src.quote: the statement should comprise a subject, a verb and a complement.

explanation.fr: Elle impose le **comment** (une technologie) au lieu du **quoi** : elle n'est pas **abstraite**, c'est-à-dire indépendante de l'implémentation.

Requirements should state 'what' is needed, not 'how".

statement.fr: Un ensemble d'exigences est jugé complet quand il ne contient plus de TBx, et il doit rester borné, c'est-à-dire ne pas dépasser le périmètre de la solution visée.
statement.en: A set of requirements is judged complete when no TBx remain, and it must stay bounded, i.e. not grow beyond the scope of the intended solution.

justification.fr: VRAI : l'ensemble est **complet** sans TBx (TBD, TBS, TBR) et **borné** s'il maintient le périmètre identifié ; ces vérifications évitent le *requirements creep*.
justification.en: TRUE: the set is **complete** with no TBx (TBD, TBS, TBR) and **bounded** if it keeps the identified scope; these checks avoid *requirements creep*.

src.quote: The final set of requirements can be judged complete when no TBx are present.

question.fr: Quelle exigence contient une « échappatoire » (loophole) au sens de la norme ?
question.en: Which requirement contains a "loophole" in the sense of the standard?

options.fr: Le système doit être meilleur que l'ancien outil de facturation.
options.en: The system shall be better than the old invoicing tool.

options.fr: Le système doit exporter les rapports en PDF si possible.
options.en: The system shall export reports in PDF if possible.

options.fr: Le système doit proposer une saisie conviviale des commandes.

options.en: The system shall allow a minimal number of clicks per order.

explanation.fr: « **si possible** » (*if possible*) est une échappatoire. Les autres relèvent d'autres familles : comparatif (« meilleur que »), langage subjectif (« convivial ») et adjectif ambigu (« minimal »).
explanation.en: "**If possible**" is a loophole. The others belong to other families: comparative ("better than"), subjective language ("user friendly") and ambiguous adjective ("minimal").

src.quote: Loopholes (such as "if possible", "as appropriate", "as applicable")
Comparative phrases (such as "better than", "higher quality")
Subjective language (such as "user friendly", "easy to use", "cost effective")
Ambiguous adverbs and adjectives (such as "almost always", "significant", "minimal")

statement.fr: Selon la norme, une exigence dit ce qu'il faut (what) et non comment le faire (how) ; on évite les termes vagues comme les pronoms « it », « this », « that » et les comparatifs comme « better than ».
statement.en: According to the standard, a requirement states what is needed, not how; vague terms such as the pronouns "it", "this", "that" and comparatives such as "better than" are avoided.

justification.fr: VRAI : c'est la règle d'or (quoi, pas comment) et deux des familles de termes vagues listées par la norme (pronoms vagues, comparatifs).
justification.en: TRUE: this is the golden rule (what, not how) and two of the families of vague terms listed by the standard (vague pronouns, comparatives).

src.quote: Requirements should state 'what' is needed, not 'how".
Avoid terms that are vague and general.
Vague pronouns (such as "it", "this", "that")

statement.fr: Une exigence peut avoir une faible priorité aux yeux d'une partie prenante et pourtant être essentielle au succès du système : c'est ce qui distingue la criticité de la priorité, qui sert à savoir quelles exigences sont négociables.

justification.en: TRUE: the standard states that priority does not imply that some requirements are unnecessary, and that **criticality** flags a low-priority but essential requirement.
